rule: Code outside a method body: the caller is its location. Field/val initializer → `Type#field`; C# property accessor → `Type#Prop` (get) / `Type#Prop=` (set); Ruby setter → `Type#x=`; `static {}` block → `Type#<clinit>`. Non-lazy initializers also get an `implicit` edge from `<clinit>`/`<init>`; lazy ones do not. | `implicit`: an execution edge the language runs without a written call — `Type#<clinit>` → `Type#field` (static initializer), `Type#<init>` → `Type#field` (instance field initializer). Line = the field's line.
notes: Static field initializer: caller App.Registry#counter, plus implicit <clinit> → #counter on the field's line; instance field initializer: caller App.Registry#names, plus implicit <init> → #names. The implicit edges' callee is a definition in the scan, so they are high (tier rule: the tool matched a definition). The C# static constructor `static Registry() { }` is the type's static initializer, the C# form of Java's `static {}` block: caller App.Registry#<clinit>. The instance constructor body's caller is App.Registry#<init>. names.Add uses the field's declared type (decision A, medium).
